title: Read Assist speech reliability research
status: Research completed against 0.2.7; findings implemented in the approved 0.2.8 feature batch.

batch: Mark failed sentences red only, without new messages, icons, cards or actions
userRequirements.comparison: User observed successful reading in Chrome on a laptop. Desktop Reading Mode is the main comparison; the exact installed voice and Chrome version were not supplied.
userRequirements.originalText: Keep document text, source offsets and reading position unchanged.

conclusions: Both reported inputs fail in the app's current EnglishNormalizer before Misaki or Kokoro synthesis is called.

The existing normalizer already handles ampersands and complete numeric currency/percent tokens, but rejects residual symbols and whitespace-separated forms such as rupee sign followed by a separate amount token.
Bounded host experiments show the existing voice model can produce finite PCM for explicit symbol-name expansions. Replacing the voice model is not the first fix supported by these results.
Removing the validation guard alone would permit omissions or spurious pronunciations. Improve context-sensitive normalization and retain validation after explicit recovery.

Chrome's public code supports adopting sentence/word boundary handling and error-specific recovery. It does not reveal a universal proprietary symbol-normalization algorithm or prove the exact cause of the user's Chrome/app difference.

code.finding: Rejects residual digits, unsupported letters and symbols after expansion; symbol guard is at line 31.
Numeric currency and percentage handling matches complete tokens.
Existing planner chunks source groups and normalized text at 220 characters.
Adapter separately rejects over 510 expanded phonemes; no automatic resplitting at this boundary.
Cache key incorporates EnglishNormalizer.VERSION, currently english-6.
blockedSentence currently derives from SpeechPreparationException; genuine frontend/model errors also need sentence ownership for red marking.
Alignment-confidence rejection permits audio-only playback and is not itself failed voice generation.

hostScope.model: Existing checksum-verified Kokoro v0.19 files with native Misaki host adapter
hostScope.outputs: All four raw/explicit-word test sentences produced finite 24 kHz PCM. This is a functional synthesis observation, not a pronunciation-quality score.
hostScope.rawInputIssue: Bypassing app normalization omitted the asterisk/standalone rupee and produced an extraneous phone sequence for boy₹%& despite complete=true.
hostScope.adapterProvenance: Host adapter main.go, bridge.c, go.mod and go.sum hashes match current sources; cached provenance/build-script stamp differs due to later metadata changes.

findings.finding: Desktop Reading Mode downloads Google natural voices and uses a system voice if that download fails.
Uses language-aware Intl.Segmenter sentence and word boundaries, including safe shortening at word boundaries. Punctuation-only sentence filtering is still a TODO.
Uses a 175-character cap for remote voices to work around a particular timeout issue; this number should not replace our model-specific limits.
Handles text-too-long by splitting, invalid speech-rate arguments by resetting rate, and intentional interruptions separately from real errors; tracks stalls.

chrome.interpretation: Useful robustness patterns are public. Exact Google voice normalization and the user's observed output have not been reproduced.

otherMethodologies.name: Deterministic normalization with semantic token classes
otherMethodologies.application: Extend the existing normalizer to classify money, percentages, operators, references and ordinary punctuation before verbalization. Use compact rules for the English Android app first.
otherMethodologies.tradeoff: A full finite-state grammar runtime is a larger integration. Sparrowhawk is archived; adopt the approach rather than assuming a maintained drop-in Android dependency.

otherMethodologies.name: Semantic pronunciation hints
otherMethodologies.application: Google Cloud documents explicit interpretations for dates, numbers, currencies and aliases. Apply the same idea by generating explicit spoken text for Kokoro.
otherMethodologies.tradeoff: Our raw model pipeline does not accept SSML; do not pass markup through as if it did.

otherMethodologies.name: Unicode normalization with preserved meaning
otherMethodologies.application: Normalize known equivalent typography in the speech representation while retaining original source text. Handle superscripts, fractions and mathematical notation before destructive compatibility folding.
otherMethodologies.tradeoff: Unicode warns that indiscriminate NFKC/NFKD can erase semantic distinctions.

otherMethodologies.name: Locale-aware number spellout
otherMethodologies.application: Evaluate ICU number spellout for future locale rules and INR, paise, decimals and Indian grouping after expressions have been classified.
otherMethodologies.tradeoff: Number formatting does not identify the intended meaning of an arbitrary expression; retain explicit parsing and tests for ambiguous separators.

otherMethodologies.name: Upstream Misaki comparison
otherMethodologies.application: Upstream exposes some symbol mappings and dollar/pound/euro currency handling. This reinforces explicit front-end rules; it does not cover every symbol or replace our INR handling.
otherMethodologies.tradeoff: Upstream Python main is not identical to the app's pinned native port. Local experiments are the evidence for this app.

otherMethodologies.name: Optional platform-voice comparison
otherMethodologies.application: Benchmark an installed offline Android voice if failures remain after improving normalization.
otherMethodologies.tradeoff: Voice availability and network requirements vary. A voice change and matching alignment path require separate product and engineering evaluation; not required to fix the reported gate.

recommendedBatchWork.details: Recognize complete currency/percentage expressions first, including symbols separated by spaces. Parse attached symbol runs separately from the ordinary word. Keep sentence grammar and document text unchanged.

Use spoken names for common ambiguous residual symbols instead of rejecting the whole sentence. Omit a marker only when source structure or an explicit deterministic rule identifies decorative markup; do not blindly delete money, operators, negatives or technical names.

Retain SourceWord IDs and original offsets for every spoken expansion; normalization and alignment share one transcript. Bump normalization/recovery recipe versions so cached audio matches the new rules.

Keep existing 220-character chunking. Add resplitting at safe source boundaries for actual post-G2P phoneme-budget excess, with progress checks and bounded attempts. Do not retry deterministic bad input unchanged or treat cancellation/alignment-only failures as model failures.

recommendedBatchWork.change: Implement the requested red sentence mark
recommendedBatchWork.details: Track actual failed document/page/sentence through prefetch and chunking. Mark only that sentence red after genuine unrecovered failure; clear it after later success. Add no new recovery UI.
Use the approved Quick-settings card, reader-scoped brightness and independent warm overlay, with failure red styling still legible.

proposedRegressionCorpus: Footnote markers *, † and superscript digits with and without structural evidence
Accents, smart punctuation, OCR spacing and line-end hyphens
Long sentences and large spoken expansions near actual model limits
Repeated words and source spans across chunks
Cancellation, missing model, synthesis error, and alignment-only rejection
acceptanceCriteria: Both user examples generate audio without a preparation exception under a documented, deterministic symbol policy.
Common currencies and percentages work with or without intervening spaces; existing successful cases remain correct.
No silent loss of ordinary words, numbers or meaningful operators; listening review checks fidelity in addition to successful PCM generation.
Original text, PDF geometry, tap targets and word/sentence IDs remain stable.
Retries cannot loop indefinitely, duplicate already-played audio or block unrelated earlier sentences.
Failure marking is red only, identifies the correct sentence, and remains legible with warm light enabled.
Phone checks validate playback, alignment, cancellation and latency before publishing the combined build.
evidenceScope: Conclusions and original localEvidence describe the pre-fix commit. Post-fix evidence is recorded separately under docs/evidence/speech-symbol-research.
